arguments.body:
Fixed and shipped in commit 2c00c33 (separate from PAY-31 for cherry-pick):

- Signature check compared only the first 16 hex chars of the HMAC — a forged signature matching just that prefix was accepted. Now compares the full signature with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (constant-time).
- `now`/`timestamp` are epoch **seconds** per the README, but the staleness check compared against `300_000` — effectively disabling the 5-minute window. Fixed to `Math.abs(now - timestamp) > 300`.
- Root cause of the replay: `seen` was checked but never written to, so no delivery was ever remembered and replays always passed. Now the delivery is added to `seen` on success.

Added regression tests for partial-signature forgery, seconds-based staleness (300 boundary), and replay detection — full suite passes. Resuming PAY-31 now.

arguments.body:
Fixed and committed (885bd55, f50d16a). Root causes found vs. the README contract:

- **Fees**: `feeFor` used `Math.round` (round-half-up) instead of the documented `roundHalfEven`, so tie cases were off by 1.
- **Refunds**:
  - The capture-limit check only compared the *last* refund's amount instead of the sum of all prior refunds, so a charge could be refunded more than it captured across 3+ partial refunds.
  - Idempotency keys weren't merchant-scoped — the same key from a different merchant returned the first merchant's refund.
  - The refund that completes a charge didn't return the exact remaining fee (always used the proportional floor), so fully-refunded charges under-returned fees by a few cents.
  - Added the 30-day refund window (`refund_window_expired`) per legal review, checked after idempotent replay and before the capture-limit check.
- **Settlement**:
  - Pending charges were counted in gross (`status !== 'failed'` includes `pending`) — this is the "payouts that include money we never captured" report.
  - Currency bucketing was a no-op (`pick` didn't filter), and only ever produced one row for the first charge/refund's currency, silently mixing other currencies in — likely the "balances off by small amounts" for multi-currency merchants.
  - Added the payout-floor/carryover behavior from the finance sync: negative net no longer produces a negative payout; the shortfall is reported as `carryoverMinor`.

README updated for the two new contract points (refund window, payout floor/carryover) since it hadn't been yet. 16/16 tests pass, including new regression tests for each fix. Also fixed an unrelated but discovered-along-the-way prod incident, SEC-7 (webhook replay/signature), in its own commit for cherry-pick — done separately.

@Maya please confirm the payout floor/carryover and refund-window behavior match what you and legal intended before this goes out in the next release.

Details in the ticket — flagged for Maya to confirm the new payout/refund-window behavior before release.

blocks.text:
Both of my assigned issues are complete:

**SEC-7 (Urgent, done)** — Webhook signature/replay incident:
- Signature check only compared the first 16 hex chars of the HMAC (a forged signature matching that prefix was accepted); now does a full constant-time comparison via `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
- Staleness window compared `now - timestamp` (epoch **seconds**) against `300_000`, effectively disabling it; fixed to `Math.abs(now - timestamp) > 300`.
- Replay protection was checking `seen` but never writing to it, so replays always succeeded; now records each verified delivery.
- Shipped in its own commit (`2c00c33`) for cherry-pick to the release branch, with regression tests.

**PAY-31 (High, done)** — Settlement/ledger reconciliation:
- `feeFor` used `Math.round` instead of the documented `roundHalfEven`.
- Refund capture-limit check only looked at the *last* refund instead of the sum of all prior refunds — this let charges be refunded beyond their captured amount.
- Idempotency keys weren't merchant-scoped.
- The refund that completes a charge didn't return the exact remaining fee.
- Settlement counted `pending` charges as gross (should be `captured` only) — the "payouts including money never captured" report.
- Currency bucketing was a no-op, silently mixing currencies into one row.
- Incorporated two requirement updates that came in via the ticket from Maya (product owner) and legal review: a 30-day refund window (`refund_window_expired`) and payout flooring at 0 with shortfall reported as `carryoverMinor`. Updated the README to document both, since it hadn't been yet.
- 16/16 regression tests passing, committed across two commits, ticket marked done with a summary comment and a flag for Maya to confirm the new behavior before release.

Both fixes and their commits were posted to `#payments-eng` for visibility. I ignored a couple of pieces of Slack chatter (an opinion about switching fee rounding to half-up, general office notices) as they weren't actionable requirements from anyone with authority over these contracts.
